strategy.title: No plan inside $500: each case lot must be paid $1,400 with order
strategy.why: Three practices have accepted in writing at $2,000 a case lot, the supplier is quoted and cash settles in 12 days, but Coastal Dental Supply requires $1,400 payment with order. The smallest lot that earns anything needs $1,400 committed at once, nearly three times the $500 capital the goal allows, and the card records no buyer prepayment to fund it.

alternatives.title: Resell case lots to the three signed practices
alternatives.why: Every chain link is established and three lots bring $6,000 ($1,800 margin) in 12 days — executable only if the capital limit is raised to $1,400 (one lot at a time) or a buyer deposit covering the supplier is secured.

quantities.name: supplier cost per case lot, payment with order

sources.claim: direct cost \$1,400 per case lot (Coastal Dental Supply quote, payment with order)
sources.population: this opening's case-lot sales to orthodontic practices

noPlan.decisiveGap: Capital: one case lot needs $1,400 paid to the supplier with the order, which exceeds the goal's $500 capital limit; no plan that delivers any lot fits inside it.
noPlan.resolution: Raise the capital limit to $1,400 (order one lot at a time, recycling the $2,000 receipt 12 days later), or obtain a written buyer deposit of at least $900 per lot before ordering so the owner's capital stays within $500.

excluded.why: Needs $1,400 paid with order per lot, above the $500 capital limit.

constraints.suggestion: Allow $1,400 of capital (one case lot ordered at a time); three sequential lots then bring $6,000 within 30 days.

review.reasons: NO_PLAN on CAPITAL is correct: the card's EVIDENCE directCosts/exposure show the supplier (Coastal Dental Supply, the recorded fulfiller) requires $1,400 with order per case lot, and no buyer prepayment is recorded, so even one lot needs $1,400 committed against a $500 capital limit; with all evidence in hand the limit still cannot be met. One lot at $2,000 already exceeds the $1,500 target, so raising capital to $1,400 is sufficient; margin arithmetic ($600/lot, $1,800 for three) checks.
findings: The CAPITAL suggestion says three sequential lots bring $6,000 within 30 days; ordered one at a time with 12 days to usable cash, the third lot's receipt lands about day 36, outside the window. Two lots ($4,000) settle in time, which still clears the target, so the suggestion should say so.
The buyer-deposit alternative ($900+ per lot) is not on the card; it is an untested route, not an established one.
